inventory_boundary.reason: The complete paper was audited through Supplement Fig. S10 and the end of the simulation section.

acceptance_criteria: C001 distinguishes the literal printed hopping direction from the conjugate-corrected Hermitian operator.
C002 searches a frozen finite domain of odd sizes and integer m for spectrum and endpoint-transfer counterexamples without treating the search as an analytic all-integer proof.
C003 verifies Schur-complement convergence of the low-energy branch to the half-length PST spectrum.
C004 checks isospectrality, endpoint support and the explicit local phase gauge of the Bell state.

D001 cross-checks the ideal static construction with two propagators, tests square/shared/channel-split pulse interpretations, then fails closed only on the undisclosed channel-resolved flattop timing contract.
No successful code attestation promotes scientific coverage or reads source graphics, author arrays, author code, paper PDF, or legacy outputs.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: The printed nearest-neighbour XY Hamiltonian is Hermitian under the stated ladder-operator convention
quantitative_claims.reason: The literal printed operator is non-Hermitian while the conjugate-corrected XY exchange is Hermitian; this is registered as a paper-error candidate pending fresh independent adjudication.

quantitative_claims.source_ref: Main Eqs. (2)-(9) and Supplement Sec. 5, PDF pp. 3-4 and 14-15
quantitative_claims.scientific_object: The zig-zag Hamiltonian realizes perfect state transfer for every allowed integer m
quantitative_claims.reason: A frozen finite-domain counterexample search supports the spectrum and transfer property, but it does not replace an analytic proof for every integer m.

quantitative_claims.source_ref: Main Eqs. (10)-(11) and Supplement Sec. 5, PDF pp. 4 and 15
quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Eliminating even sites at large m yields the stated half-length PST chain
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent Schur-complement calculations show the low-energy spectrum converging to the printed half-chain limit as m increases.

quantitative_claims.source_ref: Main Eq. (12), Fig. 3 discussion and Supplement Sec. 4, PDF pp. 5 and 12-13
quantitative_claims.scientific_object: The isospectral FST deformation produces the claimed remote Bell state with a declared phase gauge
quantitative_claims.reason: The deformation is isospectral and produces equal endpoint support; a declared local phase flip reconciles the generated Bell-plus convention with the named Bell-minus state.
